findings.title: `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is always False for `SpawnProcess`, preventing process kill/terminate
findings.body:
Processes are created via `self.mp_context.Process` where `self.mp_context = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")`, which produces `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` instances. In Python's `multiprocessing` module, `SpawnProcess` inherits from `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.Process` (`multiprocessing.context.Process`), so `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` always evaluates to `False` at runtime.

As a consequence:
1. In `_ensure_processes_alive` (line 254), `process.kill()` is never called when a flusher process hangs, leaking the hung process while spawning a replacement process for the same shards (which can also cause concurrent flushing of the same shards if the hung process recovers).
2. In `join` (line 346), `process.terminate()` is never called when shutting down.

Use `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess)` (or `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`) instead.

findings.title: `join()` breaks out of the loop on timeout without terminating remaining processes
findings.body: In `join()`, `deadline` is shared across all processes in `self.processes`. If the first process takes the full timeout to exit (or hangs until `deadline`), then on the next iteration `remaining_time = deadline - time.time()` is `<= 0` and line 341 executes `break`, exiting the loop immediately without terminating any of the remaining alive processes in `self.processes`.

findings.title: `get_memory_info()` is called redundantly for every flusher process on each `submit()`
findings.body: `SpansBuffer.get_memory_info()` queries memory usage across the Redis cluster nodes independent of which shard subset a `SpansBuffer` instance is assigned. Calling `buffer.get_memory_info()` in a loop over `self.buffers.values()` queries every Redis cluster node `num_processes` times on each `submit()` call instead of once using the main `buffer` instance.

findings.title: Inconsistent `shards` vs `shard` metric tag key and high-cardinality tag values
findings.body: Lines 185 and 195 emit metrics with `tags={"shard": shard_tag}`, whereas line 199 emits `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` with `tags={"shards": shard_tag}`. Additionally, when multiple shards share a process (such as with the default `--flusher-processes=1`), `shard_tag = ",".join(map(str, shards))` produces a comma-joined list of all partitions assigned to the consumer, which changes across consumer rebalances and creates high-cardinality tag values.

findings.title: `time.sleep(0.1)` in `test_basic` is a no-op because `time.sleep` is monkeypatched
findings.body: Line 15 monkeypatches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None`, so calling `time.sleep(0.1)` on line 62 does not actually sleep or wait for the background flusher thread to run after `current_drift` is updated. `step.join()` then immediately sets `stopped.value = True`, which can race with the background thread and cause it to exit before flushing the segment.
